correctness.rationale: Odd parts can repeat, even parts cannot, and S(0)=1. Requiring odd parts through 2m-1 and excluding 2m+1 gives the factor q^(m^2)(1-q^(2m+1)); weighting by 2m+1 and telescoping gives F=(E(q^4)/E(q)) Theta(q). Jacobi and Gauss give F=Psi(-q) R^2, with R=E(q^2)^3/(E(q)^2 E(q^4))=prod_{a>=1}(1+2q^a/(1+q^(2a))). For R=1+2U, each positive-index coefficient of U modulo 2 is the number of odd divisors of that index, which is odd exactly when the odd part is a square. Frobenius gives U^2=U(q^2) modulo 2; in U+U(q^2) the indices with positive 2-adic exponent cancel. Hence R^2=1+4 sum_{s>0 odd} q^(s^2) modulo 8. At each coefficient the sign in the correction times 4 disappears modulo 8, giving the stated formula and valuation alternatives including the constant term. If C(n)>0, 8n+1=(2j+1)^2+8s^2 has even valuation at each prime p=5 or 7 modulo 8, since -8 is a nonresidue there and any divisibility forces both coordinates to be divisible by p. For each such prime the density of even valuation is (1-1/p) sum_{a>=0}p^(-2a)=p/(p+1); truncation errors are bounded by the density of divisibility by a high p-power, and CRT multiplies densities for finitely many primes. Their product tends to zero by divergence of the prime reciprocal sum. Triangular indices also have density zero, so 8 divides S(n) on a set of natural density one. The frozen verification notes, output and code were inspected but the code was not run. A separate direct enumeration checked n=0..24 over 3,721 admissible partitions without mismatch. The finite checks do not prove the congruence or density.
